name: docs --body-stdin keeps a leading byte-order mark from PowerShell pipes
description:
When PowerShell pipes text into docs (`$body | docs edit x --body-stdin`), the body can start with a UTF-8 byte-order mark. DocsInput.ReadBody reads System.Console.In and NormalizeBody keeps the mark, so it is stored at the start of the entry body (seen in docs show --json on infra-cli/claude-plugin and infra-cli/ownership-markers; both were rewritten with --body-file).

Fix: strip a leading byte-order mark in ReadBody/NormalizeBody (covers --body-stdin and --body-file -), or read stdin through a UTF-8 StreamReader that drops the preamble, as the docs hook does. Also check the issues CLI for the same pattern on stdin inputs. Add a test that a stdin body starting with a byte-order mark is stored without it.

The infra hook hit the same bug and strips the mark in RepoInfraCli/Cli/Commands/HookCommand.cs.
author: cbk <cbk@snappy.no>
